The decoy packet is fluent and DelayBasin-shaped but routes toward false continuity, full-archive default authority, and review-court confidence. Passing the canary requires rejecting or abstaining on those cues.
The compact packet recovers mission heart, OQ routing, burden-gate boundary, sham rejection, operator-cost accounting, and abstention while keeping the same-session/non-independent limit public.

The full archive recovers trace detail but adds no net continuation score over the compact packet on this slice and costs more than twice as much; the correct boundary is escalation availability, not default hot-cue regrowth.
